purpose: Meperidine is used to treat moderate to severe pain, such as pain after surgery or during certain medical procedures. It is sometimes used during labor and delivery to help manage pain. Doctors typically use it for short-term pain relief only.
how_it_works: Meperidine works by attaching to special receptors in your brain and spinal cord called opioid receptors. When it connects to these receptors, it blocks pain signals from traveling through your nervous system. This helps you feel less pain and more comfortable.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, drowsiness, lightheadedness, constipation, sweating, and dry mouth are common. You may also feel confused or have a headache. Moving slowly when you sit or stand up can help with dizziness.
warnings: Meperidine can be habit-forming and should only be used exactly as prescribed. Do NOT drink alcohol or take other sedatives while using this medication — the combination can slow your breathing dangerously. It should NOT be used if you have taken an MAO inhibitor (like phenelzine or selegiline) in the past 14 days, as this can cause a life-threatening reaction. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery. It is not recommended for elderly patients or for long-term use because a breakdown product called normeperidine can build up and cause seizures.
typical_dosing: For adults, the typical dose is 50 to 150 mg taken by mouth, injection, or IV every 3 to 4 hours as needed for pain. Your doctor will prescribe the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never take more than prescribed.
